comments.body_html:
Thanks a lot for the mod. One question I already had back with CactusPies’ mod, but never asked.

I assume the mod uses the player positions’ x,y coordinates retrieved from the game to place/planar project the marker on the map.

Isn’t it possible to also retrieve the z (height) coordinate and simply transform that to different mini map coordinates, i.e. if you have a z value of 0, place the marker as it’s done now, if you have a z value of e.g. >10, that means e.g. next height level, instead of drawing the marker at the same position as with z=0, transform it to the part of the map which shows that location.

E.g. for Interchange it could look like this (assuming height values in meters):

z=0 -> normal marker position, ground level, i.e. parking garage

z>=10 -> 1st level

z>=20 -> 2nd level

I know Interchange is an easy example, compared to Reserve. But couldn’t it be at least an option to toggle for specific maps?

comments.author: TechHappy
comments.body_html:
No need for any other tools like Hamachi. The devices just need to be on the same network. The easy way to view the map on a mobile device is to open the browser map using the computer, pressing the “QR Code” button, and scanning that QR code using the mobile device camera. If you want to open the map directly from the phone without scanning the code, you will need to type into the address bar the computer’s local IP address followed by the configured port (default 8080) and then “/index.html”.

The URL that I use for example is: “http://192.16.1.103:8080/index.html”

comments.author: TechHappy
comments.body_html: I am glad that you got it to work. I do want to say though that the IP address that websites give you is your router’s public IP, not your computer’s IP on the network. You can’t connect using the public IP. To find the computer’s IP, use the “ipconfig” command in a Windows Command Prompt.
